title: Red lentil dal tadka
intro: Silky red lentils topped with a sizzling tempering of spices, garlic and onion.

steps.t: Rinse the lentils in a sieve until the water runs clear.
Put them in a pot with the water, turmeric and chopped tomato; bring to the boil and skim off the foam.
Simmer, half covered, stirring now and then, until the lentils collapse and turn creamy.
steps.label: Lentils

pressure.t: Pressure cooker: lock the lid and cook 8 minutes at high pressure, then let the pressure drop naturally.

steps.t: Meanwhile, make the tadka: heat the oil in a small pan and fry the chopped onion until golden.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the cumin, mustard seeds, sliced garlic, ginger and chillies and cook until the seeds pop and the garlic is golden.
steps.label: Tadka

steps.t: When the lentils are ready, salt them and whisk until smooth; loosen with hot water if too thick.
Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal, add lemon and coriander and serve with rice.

tips.t: Pour the tadka over at the very last moment, still sizzling: that's where all the aroma is.
Serve with basmati rice and a cucumber and red onion salad.

title: Tofu and broccoli stir-fry
intro: Crispy tofu and broccoli tossed in a glossy soy, ginger and garlic sauce.

steps.t: Pat the tofu dry, cut it into 2 cm cubes and toss in most of the cornflour.
Mix the soy, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, water and the rest of the cornflour: that's the sauce.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat and fry the tofu, turning, until golden and crisp; set aside.
steps.label: Tofu

airfryer.t: Air-fry the coated tofu at 200°C for 12 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp.

steps.t: Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the broccoli florets and pepper strips with a splash of water until bright green.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Add the chopped garlic, ginger and white part of the spring onions and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce, return the tofu and toss until the sauce thickens and coats everything.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Finish with sesame seeds and the green spring onion; serve with rice.

tips.t: Press the tofu under a weight for 15 minutes first: it loses water and crisps up better.
Add toasted cashews and a teaspoon of chilli flakes for a richer version.

title: Lentil meatballs in tomato sauce
intro: Soft lentil and carrot balls, baked and then simmered in tomato sauce.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200°C. Drain the lentils and pat them very dry with kitchen paper.

airfryer.t: Preheat the air fryer to 190°C. Drain the lentils and pat them very dry with kitchen paper.

steps.t: Blend half the lentils and mash the rest; add grated carrot, breadcrumbs, parsley, tomato paste, oregano, salt and pepper.
Knead and let it rest so the breadcrumbs soak up the moisture.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Shape 16 balls, set them on a lined tray and brush with 2 tbsp oil.
Bake, turning halfway, until golden and firm.
steps.label: Oven

airfryer.t: Air-fry at 190°C for 15 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.

steps.t: Meanwhile, warm the tomato sauce (store-bought is fine) with the remaining oil in a wide pan.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Lay the balls in the sauce and let them soak up the flavour without stirring; just shake the pan.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Finish with basil and serve.

tips.t: Dry the lentils well: the drier they are, the less breadcrumb you need and the softer they stay.
They keep 3 days in the fridge in their sauce; great cold in a sandwich too.
A teaspoon of cumin or smoked paprika in the mix changes their whole character.

title: Black bean chili
intro: Thick, smoky vegan chili with black beans, corn and red pepper.

steps.t: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the chopped onion and pepper over medium heat until soft.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Add the garlic, cumin, chilli, paprika and oregano and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes, beans, corn and water; salt and bring to the boil.
Simmer uncovered over low heat, stirring now and then, until thick.
steps.label: Chili

slow.t: Transfer everything to the slow cooker, cover and cook on low for 4 hours.

steps.t: Mash a few ladlefuls of beans against the pot to make it creamier.
Add the lime juice, check the salt and serve with coriander and rice.

tips.t: A square of dark chocolate at the end adds depth without making it sweet.
Serve with rice, diced avocado and toasted corn tortillas.
Freezes perfectly in portions; even better reheated the next day.

title: Spinach and chickpeas, Seville style
intro: Chickpeas and spinach bound with a paste of fried bread, garlic, cumin and paprika.

steps.t: Wash the spinach and wilt it in a wide pan with a splash of water, then drain and squeeze dry.
steps.label: Spinach

steps.t: In the same pan, fry the bread and whole garlic cloves in 3 tbsp oil until golden.
steps.label: Bread & garlic

steps.t: Pound them in a mortar, or blend, with the cumin, paprika, vinegar and a pinch of salt into a thick paste.
Heat the remaining oil, add the paste and drained chickpeas and stir for 1 minute.
Add the roughly chopped spinach and the water and cook over low heat until the sauce coats the chickpeas.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.

tips.t: The fried bread, garlic and spice paste is what binds the dish: don't skip it.
Use chard instead of spinach for a more rustic version.
Tastier the next day: reheat with a splash of water.

title: Gemista (stuffed vegetables)
intro: Tomatoes and peppers stuffed with herby rice, baked with potatoes.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 190°C. Slice the tops off the tomatoes and peppers and keep them; scoop out the tomatoes with a teaspoon.
Blend the tomato pulp, deseed the peppers and salt the inside of the vegetables.
Fry the chopped onion, garlic and grated courgette in half the oil over medium heat until soft.
steps.label: Soffritto

steps.t: Add the rice and half the blended pulp and cook, stirring, until the rice absorbs the liquid.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Take off the heat and stir in the parsley, mint, oregano, salt and pepper.
Fill the vegetables three-quarters full, put the tops back on and set them in a baking dish.
Tuck the potato wedges around them, pour over the rest of the pulp and oil and season.
Cover with foil and bake.
steps.label: Covered bake

steps.t: Uncover and bake until the rice is tender and the vegetables are golden and wrinkled.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it rest before serving: it's even better warm.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Fill only three-quarters full: the rice swells as it cooks and would split the vegetables.
If you're not vegan, a slab of feta and bread on the side are the classic partners.
Even better the next day at room temperature; keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Mushroom goulash
intro: Browned mushrooms stewed with onions, paprika and caraway, German style.

steps.t: Wipe the mushrooms clean and cut them into large pieces; slice the onions and pepper.
Brown the mushrooms in 2 tbsp oil in a wide pot over high heat, in batches, until golden; set aside.
steps.label: Mushrooms

steps.t: Lower the heat, add the remaining oil, the onions and pepper and cook until soft and golden.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, caraway and marjoram; then take off the heat and stir in both paprikas.
Pour in the vegetable stock (store-bought is fine), return the mushrooms, salt and simmer until thick.
steps.label: Goulash

steps.t: Season with salt and pepper, scatter with parsley and serve with boiled potatoes.

tips.t: Take the pot off the heat before adding the paprika: if it burns it turns bitter.
Serve with boiled potatoes, soft polenta or bread dumplings.

title: Fagioli all'uccelletto
intro: Tuscan cannellini beans stewed with tomato, garlic and sage: simple and full of flavour.

steps.t: In a pot, ideally earthenware, warm the oil with crushed garlic and sage over low heat until the sage is crisp.
steps.label: Sage

steps.t: Add the crushed tomatoes, salt and cook until the sauce reduces.
steps.label: Tomatoes

steps.t: Add the beans and water, stir gently and cook over low heat until the sauce is thick and creamy.
steps.label: Beans

steps.t: Remove the garlic, adjust the salt, grind over black pepper and finish with a drizzle of raw oil.
Let them rest for a few minutes and serve hot.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: With home-cooked dried beans and a ladle of their cooking water, the sauce turns creamier.
In Tuscany they're served with grilled sausages or on slices of toasted bread.
